run.answer:
## Review summary

- **CloudBox:** The $79.99 annual renewal posted on October 1, within the 14-day refund window stated in the trial notice. I submitted a refund request; case **CB-1001**. The note says the plan is no longer needed, so I saved a waiting case requesting your approval to cancel it. **The plan is not cancelled.**
- **Harbor Bank:** I submitted a request for a courtesy reversal of two $35 overdraft fees dated September 11 and 12, totaling **$70**, and asked the bank to confirm they are separate valid fees. Reference **HB-1002**.
- **ShopMart:** The two September 17 charges, **$31.85** and **$59.60**, match the order confirmation. The promised **$53.73** return refund posted September 9. No further ShopMart request was indicated.
- **Recurring charges saved for review:** Metro Power (latest $133.02/month), Spotify ($11.99/month), and Oakview Apartments ($1,625/month). I found no note saying these are unused; I did not request changes.
- I scheduled follow-ups for CloudBox and Harbor Bank on October 20. The posted transaction history does not show either new refund or reversal yet.

verify_run.answer:
Found $70 in Harbor Bank overdraft fees and a $79.99 CloudBox renewal refund. Both credits posted on October 15, and I recorded them as received. CloudBox also says the account is closed; I left the cancellation approval case open because the saved case requires your approval before any service change.

ShopMart’s $53.73 return posted. The promised $24.31 refund for order SM-52802 did not appear, so I saved an opportunity and follow-up. Its support page failed to load, which blocked submission. The two September ShopMart orders match their receipts, so no request was needed.

I also found regular charges for Spotify, Metro Power, and Oakview Apartments. I found no evidence in the notes reviewed that these are unwanted, so I took no service action.
